scope: Development-exposed model hypothesis; all prior errors known; not prospective or independent validation.
hypothesis: A fixed oxidized full-scaffold reference and methyl-nicotinamide redox transfer can retain useful local redox estimates while assigning one potential per molecular input.
selection: Single N-ribosyl 1,4-dihydronicotinamide with primary amide; exact same atom-index spectators, stereochemistry and phosphate state; no reaction or label routing. Other molecules retain the full reference policy.
reference_choice: Oxidized sibling fixed by ring oxidation, not energy or label comparison. No fitted constants, regression, cycle projection, amino-acid model changes, extra counterions or solvent changes.
sampling: Expand each virtual molecular energy into shared raw primitives and combine derivatives before quadrature. This excludes locality, protonation and solvation model error.
conditions: Inherited full-molecule v2 T298.15K,pH7,I0,noMg,1Msolute,wateractivity1; unsupported declarations refused.
outcomes: All364requests and mutually exclusive status categories
Conditional all-available and paired-common MAE/RMSE/bias/>20errors versus zero
Shared state signatures across reactions and independent opposite-order population
Reversal, extent2, atomorder, speciesorder invariance on all successful candidate requests
Complete nullspace closure for available literal-input/pool stoichiometry including explicit protons
adoption_rule: No production promotion from development MAE. A locality approximation requires external evidence for redox and scaffold exchange/biosynthesis; remaining routes also require consistent repair.
failure_policy: No missing-reference fallback to the previous context-dependent route; retain all missing/unsupported requests. No label removal based on prediction or error.
external_labels: Zero new independent labels admitted. Existing Mg-bounded labels are development exposed and condition-approximated. No confirmatory p-values.
resources: Pure owned-record CPU reassembly on CPU79, native threads1, no GPU or quantum recomputation; no fleet submission.
